newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly steady but LSFO still soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly steady but LSFO still soft.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady again Tuesday in lackluster trade, but low sulphur sentiment remained bearish amid crumbling gas prices and forecasts for very mild East Coast weather this week.
"With gas crashing, sellers are starting to lower their numbers," said one East Coast utility buyer, noting the recent slide in natgas prices triggered fuel switching from resid.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged from Friday at about $16.25-50 a barrel, with March one percent paper also little changed at $16.40-65 and April paper flat at $16.30-60, traders said.

But NYH 0.3 percent high pour continued to erode, down another 50 cents to $17.25, as sellers again were forced to lower expectations amid city gate gas prices in the sub-$14 a barrel equivalent range.
NYH high sulphur grades were stable, with 2.2 percent still in the low-$15 area.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent grade held steady at about $15.25, while three percent was up 25-50 cents to $12.75 on reports two damaged coker units were repaired.
"Some of the USG refinery problems are over, but there's still no demand," said one cash trader, noting winter was almost over.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices tumbled almost 50 cents to the $2.15-20/mmBtu level versus NYH one percent resid still at a $2.60/mmBtu equivalent.
